title: Paneer Jalfrezi
subtitle: A dry, tangy curry of paneer, peppers, and spiced tomato
excerpt: Jalfrezi is a stir-fry style curry with a thick, punchy sauce. Paneer holds its shape in the heat and takes on colour where it touches the pan. Peppers and onion keep some crunch throughout.
sourceNotes: Anglo-Indian restaurant tradition; jalfrezi is closely associated with British-Indian curry-house cooking.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The tomato-spice base can be made a day ahead. Add the paneer and peppers when reheating so they keep their texture.

content.text: Jalfrezi is a dry curry cooked over high heat, closer to a stir-fry than a slow-simmered sauce. The paneer benefits from a quick fry first so it gets a golden crust. Do not let the peppers go limp as the crunch is part of the dish.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a wide pan over high heat. Add the paneer cubes in a single layer. Fry for 2 minutes per side until golden. Remove and set aside.
Add the remaining oil to the same pan. Add the cumin seeds and let them sizzle for 20 seconds. Add the onion and fry for 5 minutes over medium-high heat until softened and lightly coloured.
Add the garlic and ginger. Stir for one minute. Add the turmeric, coriander, and chilli powder. Stir for 30 seconds.
Add the tomato puree and tinned tomatoes. Cook over medium heat for 8 minutes, stirring often, until the sauce thickens and the oil starts to separate at the edges.
Add the sliced peppers. Stir and cook for 4 minutes. The peppers should soften slightly at the edges but keep their crunch.
Return the paneer to the pan. Stir gently to coat. Season with salt. Add the garam masala and stir through.
Scatter over fresh coriander. Serve with rice or flatbreads.

items.symptom: The paneer is soft and falls apart when stirred.
items.cause: It was not fried first, or it was old and wet.
items.fix: Pat the paneer dry before frying. Frying it first in hot oil firms the outside and helps it hold its shape in the sauce.

items.symptom: The sauce is too wet and coats nothing.
items.cause: The tomatoes were not reduced enough.
items.fix: Cook the tomato base until you can see the oil pooling at the edges and the sauce pulls away from the sides of the pan.

items.cause: They went in too early or cooked too long.
items.fix: Add the peppers in the last 4 minutes only. Keep the heat high so they colour a little rather than stew.
